subject: Sprint 3 round-two repair of the governed answer() surface: inverted merge rule, numeric-divergence and structural-divergence conflict signals, additive evidenced absence (working tree against 41476a6)
summary: Both prior round-two High findings are independently confirmed repaired, and generally rather than shape-bound. S3-R-10 was re-derived with four constructed same-authority contradiction shapes that reuse no fixture wording, and BOTH halves of the fix hold: each yields exactly one Conflict and two singly-cited claims, and with lee_kb.answer.detect_conflicts neutralized each still yields two unmerged claims, so the merge refusal does not depend on detection. S3-R-11 was re-derived with a control/treatment pair in which a short, same-topic, top-ranked CANONICAL 'does not exist' record joins the answer as its own singly-cited claim while both substantive claims survive with their citations and nothing is demoted to evidence_omitted. Reconciliation, governed exclusivity, citation and receipt closure, absence distinguishability, derived confidence, the dependency boundary and the disclosure surface all survived independent probing repository-wide. One High finding is introduced by this round: the previously undocumented structural-divergence branch in _conflict_signal reports agreement as disagreement whenever two same-topic statements exceed 0.5 meaningful-term Jaccard with unequal term sets. Measured with an identical probe and corpora against the working tree and a git archive HEAD copy of the pre-repair tree, 5 of 6 constructed non-competing pairs now emit a Conflict against 1 of 6 pre-repair; it reaches the project's own benchmark corpus (family 7 harbor readiness, 3 conflicts pre to 4 post, one between a statement and the audit source that says it confirms it) and is user-visible through the shipped lee-kb ask command. A second, Medium documentation finding: docs/answer-benchmark-results.md never names that branch, misattributes two of the three new family-5d fixtures to antonym handling when they actually fire it, and reports the family-7 confidence-distribution change while omitting the conflict-count change on the same question.

findings.location: src/lee_kb/answer_conflict.py:259-267 (_conflict_signal structural-divergence branch), :85 _STRUCTURAL_DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD, :317 _statements_mergeable; user-visible at src/lee_kb/main.py:568-577
findings.problem: The branch this round added at the end of _conflict_signal emits "Competing statements about ... differ in meaningful terms." whenever two same-topic statements have a meaningful-term Jaccard of at least 0.5 AND unequal term sets. Set inequality is not disagreement, so mere difference is reported as conflict. Independently measured (probe E: six constructed non-competing pairs, each written to two same-authority source roots, discovered through the real LocalFilesConnector into real SQLite, then the identical probe and corpora re-run against a git archive HEAD (41476a6) copy of the pre-repair tree): 5 of 6 agreeing pairs now emit a Conflict, against 1 of 6 pre-repair. 'The platform team owns the Perseus runbook.' vs 'The Perseus runbook is owned by the platform team.' -- identical meaning, differing only in voice -- is reported as competing, because owns != owned (Jaccard 0.667). So is 'The Halcyon policy retains audit logs.' vs the same sentence plus 'under section 4.', where one side is a strict elaboration of the other (0.625), and 'The Vega ingest queue runs in the north region.' against the same sentence plus a time qualifier (0.667). The defect is reachable from the project's own benchmark fixtures: probe F rebuilds the twelve-document primary corpus and asks the five family-7 questions; 'What does harbor readiness require from the cobalt checklist?' now emits a conflict between the duplicate-repository statement and the independent-audit statement whose own text reads 'The independent audit confirms that harbor readiness requires the cobalt checklist.' Family-7 conflicts go from 3 pre-repair to 4 post-repair on the identical corpus. Reproduced end to end through the shipped CLI: lee-kb sync then lee-kb ask "Who owns the Perseus runbook?" prints both agreeing statements as two directly_evidenced claims and then lists them under a Conflicts: heading with 'newer: neither; more authoritative: neither'. The suite cannot catch this: the only negative fixture, tests/test_answer_conflict.py:208, uses a pair at Jaccard 0.4 -- below the 0.5 gate -- so it passes without ever exercising the branch, and no fixture asserts that agreeing statements produce no conflict. Two of the three new family-5d fixtures (enabled-versus-turned-off at exactly 0.500, permitted-versus-forbidden at 0.600) pass through this same undiscriminating branch, not through any antonym test, so they green-light the defect rather than bounding it. Calibration, stated plainly: no claim text is wrong, nothing is suppressed, every citation still resolves, and the failure direction is over-warning rather than under-warning -- on claim-level correctness alone this would be Medium, and the prior review rated its narrower pre-existing form (S3-R-12) Medium. It is filed High because this round widened it fivefold on constructed non-competing pairs, moved it into the benchmark corpus's own published results, and made it user-visible on the only shipped surface: a reader cannot tell which entries under Conflicts: are real disagreements, and a machine consumer filtering on conflicts receives mostly noise.
findings.proposed_fix: Require a positive contradiction signal instead of set inequality. (a) Treat a strict superset of meaningful terms as elaboration, not divergence, and apply the same superset rule to _value_words_diverge, which also closes the pre-existing S3-R-12 Corvus shape. (b) Normalize light morphology (owns/owned, list/listed, retains/retained) before comparing term sets, so a paraphrase is not a disagreement -- _KNOWN_SYNONYM_SETS already has the right shape and only needs to stop being a two-entry hand list. (c) Gate the branch on a genuine substitution: both sides must supply distinct fillers for the same slot in an otherwise matching frame (both a number, both a value word, both a proper noun), rather than merely differing. (d) Add permanent regression fixtures for agreeing pairs -- elaboration, voice change, added qualifier -- each asserting result.conflicts == (), and pin the expected conflict count for the family-7 harbor-readiness question, so this class cannot regress silently again. Raising _STRUCTURAL_DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD alone is not a fix: the Kestrel fixture sits at exactly 0.500 and would break first.
findings.evidence: probeE_falsepositive.py run against both trees (5/6 vs 1/6 agreeing pairs flagged; the pre-repair tree additionally MISSES the control contradiction); probeF_benchmark_corpus.py run against both trees (family-7 conflicts 4 post vs 3 pre, claims 11 vs 10); inline probe G branch attribution (Kestrel 0.500 structural, Vega 0.600 structural, Lyra 0.667 numeric, harbor 0.625 structural, elaboration 0.625 structural, voice change 0.667 structural); lee-kb sync + lee-kb ask reproduction, both exit 0.

findings.problem: The benchmark document describes this round's conflict-detection work as two changes -- inverting the merge rule and adding a numeric-divergence signal -- and never mentions the third, the meaningful-term structural-divergence branch. Probe G measures which branch actually fires for each fixture: the numeric signal fires only for Lyra; Kestrel and Vega both fire the structural branch. The document nonetheless describes those two as reproducing 'the same shape for antonym pairs outside the fixed vocabulary', when the branch that catches them performs no antonym test at all and fires identically on elaboration and voice change. Family 5d's stated guarantee is therefore true as measured but is not evidence of the property the row claims to prove. Separately, the document reports the family-7 behaviour change it likes (10 claims to 11; SYNTHESIZED 9+1 to 11+0 -- probe F reproduces both figures exactly, pre and post) but not the change on the same question that it does not: conflicts 3 to 4. And Recommendation section 1 still presents S3-R-12 as the single narrow remaining conflict defect, scoped to the value-word and authority branches, when a broader one now ships; the closing paragraph's assertion that no confidently-wrong-output defect remains no longer holds. The recommendation value, 'Ready after specific follow-up', matches what I observe; its stated justification does not, and a reader using this document to decide whether to release would understate the open correctness surface.
findings.proposed_fix: Name the structural-divergence branch in the revision summary and in the family 5d row, and describe what it actually tests (term-set inequality above a similarity floor), not antonymy. Report the family-7 conflict-count change alongside the confidence-distribution change, since both come from the same repair on the same question. Replace Recommendation section 1 with S3-R-15, noting S3-R-12 as its narrower subset, and drop the closing sentence's implication that no confidently-wrong-output defect remains.
findings.evidence: probeF_benchmark_corpus.py against both trees reproduces every figure the document states (11 claims all directly_evidenced, 0 unresolved, post; 9+1=10, pre) and also the unreported conflict delta 3 -> 4; inline probe G attributes each fixture to its firing branch.

The LLM-backed SynthesisProvider is specified but unimplemented, pending dependency approval: answer() ships only DeterministicSynthesisProvider, a standard-library template renderer with no model call, so lee-kb ask returns template prose rather than natural-language synthesis. Verified rather than assumed: pyproject.toml project.dependencies is [], an AST walk over all 31 tracked Python files finds pytest as the only non-stdlib import in the repository, and a 22-term model-client class scan over all 98 tracked files returns exactly one hit in src/tests/tools -- the English word 'requests' in a governance.py error string.

Live filesystem verification is deferred: every result in this review, in docs/answer-benchmark-results.md and in the delivered suite comes from temporary synthetic projections, including my own probes. Nothing exercises answer() against a live, continuously-synchronized filesystem corpus over time -- freshness drift, resync during use, tombstoning mid-question, concurrent sync are all unmeasured.

answer() has still never been run against the real ~1,213-document corpus (Open Question 7). S3-R-15 is corpus-shape sensitive in the direction that matters: a real policy corpus contains far more near-duplicate restatements, elaborations and cross-references than fourteen fixtures do, so I expect its false-conflict incidence there to be materially higher than the single instance visible in the benchmark corpus.

The suite still cannot catch the defect it was written beside: S3-R-15 survives a green 245-test suite and a green 19/19 benchmark run, exactly as S3-R-10 and S3-R-11 survived a green 241-test suite. Each round's fixtures pin the shape the finding was reported against; the round's new behaviour goes unpinned in the opposite direction. Negative fixtures asserting what must NOT be reported are the missing half.

Two Sprint 1/2 open questions are inherited unchanged: OR-matcher worst-case retrieval latency (~1.521s, Open Question 5) and permission-basis on receipts (Open Question 2), both of which apply to answer() because it calls retrieve() directly.
